refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: These configuration files control the behavior of systemd-sysext8 and systemd-confext8. They are especially useful when needing to customize the behavior of the respective extension service units.

refsect1.title: Options
refsect1.para: The following options are understood in both the [SysExt] and [ConfExt] sections:

listitem.para: Set the mutable mode for system extensions. Takes one of no, yes, auto, import, ephemeral, or ephemeral-import. For details about the modes, see the --mutable= option in systemd-sysext8. Defaults to no.
Set the image policy. Takes an image policy string as argument, as per systemd.image-policy7. For details, see the --image-policy= option in systemd-sysext8.

Controls whether plain directory (or btrfs subvolume) extension images are considered. Takes a boolean or the special value auto. If true, directory images are considered regardless of where they are located. If false, directory images are never considered, and only disk images are merged. If set to auto, directory images are only considered if they are located below /usr/ or /var/, if the file system they are located on is a tmpfs (e.g. /run/), if it is backed by dm-crypt or dm-verity block devices, or if it is the same file system that backs the root directory, /usr/ or /var/ (regardless of where on that file system the directory is located). tmpfs is permitted since its contents only exist at runtime, and hence cannot be manipulated offline. This is useful to permit directory images in general, but refuse them if they are placed on unprotected storage, such as the EFI System Partition (ESP), or other file systems that are not authenticated or encrypted. Defaults to auto.

The directory policy is enforced when activating an extension, i.e. at the same time the image policy is enforced for disk images. If the directory image found under an extension name is refused, the extension name is skipped, i.e. a disk image of the same name in a directory of lower priority is not considered either. When listing extension images the directory policy is not taken into account. The --directory-policy= command line option of systemd-sysext8 takes precedence over this setting.
Note that this setting has no effect on disk image files, which are subject to ImagePolicy= instead.
